# s393 — Retract a note that turned out wrong

**Findings:** ork S65 relay, 2026-10-25 · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

A relay orchestrator recorded `Review FAIL: none (reviewer: no blockers)` on ork's S65 because a fix round ran for UI suggestions. It is not a failure, but a note cannot be withdrawn, so the slice history shows a false FAIL. `slicer note` (src/slicer/cli.py:2422) has kinds and `--stale-after` but no retraction.

## Files

- `src/slicer/cli.py:2422` (cmd_note) and the note record model.
- The render of notes and the note packing used by `next --ready`.

## Failing tests

- A retracted note stays in history with who, when and why, renders struck or dim, and is skipped by `next --ready` note packing.
- Retracting an unknown note names the item and the note reference and says what to do next.

## Implement

Proposed form: slicer note gains a retract option that takes the note reference and a reason (flag names to be decided in the slice). Never delete the note.

`python3 tests/affected.py --run`; `slicer check`.
